supersedes.reason: Independent review found permissive and mutable approval records, redirectable expected-output paths, and unhashed nontrivial prompts. This manifest records strict approval, baseline-path, prompt-identity, and Git-immutability corrections.

checks.result: The exact clean review-fix commit passed all 13 foundation commands and all 91 foundation tests.

All 10 focused tests passed, including strict approval-schema mutations, dirty and committed approval rewrites, canonical baseline confinement, prompt hashing and identity, deterministic end-to-end execution, tampering, and scratch confinement.
Both canonical golden-parsing and contract-validation benchmarks passed at the exact clean commit.
ADR validation passed with two indexed records and 28 task-scope paths inspected.

evidence: The golden metadata normalizer and strict contract validator execute offline and pass exact JSON comparison without a baseline-update command.
Expected outputs are nonredirected files at canonical evaluation/baselines/<benchmark-id>.json paths recorded in current and historical lineage.
Version 2+ changes require an exact-schema human approval whose bytes are SHA-256-pinned; tracked approval rewrites and removals fail in both dirty and committed Git states.

Ten focused tests reproduce the review attacks: extra approval keys, Boolean versions, blank human identities, approval rewrites, expected-output redirects, and real prompts without governed paths or hashes.
The complete exact-commit foundation suite has 91 passing tests.
Registry and approval schemas, prompt and approval conventions, the automation guide, and proposed ADR-0002 describe the same canonical paths, hash pins, immutability, and version rules.
The correction remains confined to evaluation governance, its runner and focused tests, documentation, prior evidence, and synchronized task audit views.
